title: Fuel Volume Regulator Control Circuit/Open
shortDescription: Open circuit detected in the fuel volume regulator solenoid.
fullDescription:
The PCM has detected an open circuit in the fuel volume regulator control. This regulator controls fuel pressure on direct-injection high-pressure fuel systems.

With an open circuit, the PCM cannot command fuel pressure, leading to drivability issues and potential safe-mode operation.
safetyImpact: Possible engine stall or loss of power.

fixSteps.title: Scan and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Read freeze frame and inspect regulator connector.

title: Fuel Volume Regulator Control Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: Fuel volume regulator circuit out of range.
fullDescription:
The PCM detects regulator performance outside expected values. Can be caused by clogged regulator, failing solenoid, or wiring resistance.

Drivability and emissions are impacted.

fixSteps.title: Measure fuel pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Compare actual vs commanded rail pressure.

title: Fuel Volume Regulator Control Circuit Low
fullDescription:
The PCM detects low voltage on the regulator control circuit — often a short to ground or failing solenoid.

Fuel delivery will be incorrect.

fixSteps.title: Check wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect for chafed harness grounding out.

title: Fuel Volume Regulator Control Circuit High
fullDescription: The control circuit shows higher voltage than expected — short to voltage or open.

title: Engine Position System Performance Bank 1
fullDescription: PCM detects the engine position system on bank 1 is not meeting expected correlation — often due to timing chain stretch.

fixSteps.title: Check cam/crank correlation

faq.a: Yes — chain failure can destroy engine.
